verdicts.evidence: The gate-side twin of the compliance anchor survivor (compliance-top-level.json, key 30|21|30|50), re-probed here on conformance.ts's own FRONTMATTER because this copy feeds parseRuleMeta — expectedRules, ruleSignatures, the verdict itself. RECIPE (2026-08-27, mutant applied to a package-shaped dist copy): shipped example + vendored runward/rules (all 64 package rules, hashes recorded in scaffold-lock.json so corpusDivergence is 'verifiable' and clean — house rules are explicitly legitimate) + one house note 'house-quoted-note.md' whose first 800 bytes are prose and which QUOTES a '---/impact: CRITICAL/phases: [architect]/---' block beyond byte 800 (past the 800-byte head corpusDivergence's own extra-rule sniff reads). MEASURED: shipped build exit 0; mutated build exit 1 — '✗ Architect · house-quoted-note — not accounted for in the Rule conformance manifest'. Dropping the anchor lets any frontmatter-shaped block anywhere in a rule file be read as frontmatter, so a prose note becomes an expected CRITICAL rule and the gate reddens a green mission — a false red the operator can only clear by writing a manifest row for a rule nobody wrote; the same mechanism can hand ruleSignatures a phantom 'signature:' quoted in prose and turn the regex screen on against text. Opposite failure direction from the compliance twin (there: coverage inflated in the pack that leaves the building), same blind spot: test/unit/frontmatter-crlf.test.js's fixtures all carry their frontmatter at byte 0, so the '^' is never load-bearing in the unit net, and audit-corpus's CRLF honest case keeps frontmatter at byte 0 too. All six full-net legs plus the self-gate replayed against the mutated build: PASS.
